summary: Applies non-linear deformations such as twist, bend, shear, taper, linear taper, and squash/stretch to point, vertex, or primitive attributes. Deformation is controlled by axes, pivot, strength, rolloff, and optional per-point weights.

key_params.name: inputattrscope
key_params.note: Input attribute or components to deform

key_params.name: weightattr
key_params.note: Weight attribute that scales strength per element

key_params.name: op
key_params.note: Twist, bend, shear, taper, linear taper, or squash/stretch

key_concepts: Twist POP performs non-linear deformation operations: twist, bend, shear, taper, linear taper, and squash/stretch.
Attribute Class and Input Attribute Scope let it deform point, vertex, or primitive attributes, not only P.
Primary axis, secondary axis, and pivot define the local deformation frame for the selected operation.
Strength sets the amount of deformation, Rolloff shapes how deformation changes away from the pivot or axes, and Weight Attribute scales strength per element.
Output Attribute Scope and output metadata allow the result to overwrite P for visible geometry motion or write a separate deformed attribute.
common_gotchas: Weight attributes multiply strength per element, so unexpected Weight values can make deformation appear missing or extreme.
Axes and pivot define the deformation frame; normalize or center geometry first when procedural inputs vary.
Deforming non-P attributes is valid, but downstream renderers usually need P changed for visible geometry motion.
